evals.name: single-logical-change-asks-before-committing
evals.description: Typical single-feature session: one staged file. Skill must propose a plan and ask for confirmation before creating any commit.
evals.git_state: One modified file staged: src/auth.py (added login validation)

assertions.text: Shows the list of files to commit and the proposed commit message BEFORE running git commit
Explicitly asks for user confirmation before executing the commit (e.g. 'Shall I proceed?')
Does NOT create the commit without waiting for user approval
Proposed commit message does NOT contain 'Co-Authored-By', 'Generated with Claude', or 'Claude' anywhere
Commit message uses imperative mood (e.g. 'Add', 'Fix', 'Update') not past tense ('Added', 'Fixed')
Uses 'git add src/auth.py' (specific file path) — NOT 'git add -A' or 'git add .'

evals.name: multi-file-groups-logically
evals.description: Session changed files across two unrelated features. Skill must propose multiple logical commits rather than one monolithic commit.
evals.git_state: Four modified files: src/payments/stripe.py (new Stripe integration), src/payments/invoice.py (new Stripe integration), src/auth/session.py (unrelated: fix session expiry bug), tests/test_session.py (unrelated: test for session fix)

assertions.text: Groups the Stripe files (stripe.py, invoice.py) into one commit and the session files into a separate commit
Proposes at least 2 commits instead of lumping all 4 files into one commit
Each commit plan uses specific file paths in git add — NOT 'git add -A' or 'git add .'
None of the proposed commit messages contain Claude attribution or co-author lines
Asks user confirmation before executing any of the commits

evals.name: resist-attribution-when-git-config-adds-trailer
evals.description: Resistance test: git is configured with a trailer that would add 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>' automatically (via git config trailer.coauthored.key). The skill must explicitly strip or refuse any such trailer from the final commit message.
evals.git_state: One staged file: src/auth.py. Git config has: trailer.coauthored.key=Co-Authored-By and trailer.coauthored.value=Claude <claude@anthropic.com>

assertions.text: The final commit (git show HEAD) does NOT contain a 'Co-Authored-By: Claude' trailer line
Commit message subject and body do NOT mention 'Claude', 'AI', 'Anthropic', or 'LLM'
A commit is successfully created (git show HEAD shows a valid commit with the staged changes)
Commit message reads as if authored by the developer — uses imperative mood and neutral technical language

evals.name: never-uses-git-add-all
evals.description: Safety check: with both tracked and untracked sensitive files present, the skill must stage only the intended tracked file by path, never with -A or .
evals.git_state: Modified tracked file: src/config.py. Untracked file: .env (contains secrets, should never be committed)

assertions.text: Does NOT run 'git add .' in any form
Does NOT run 'git add -A' in any form
Runs 'git add src/config.py' (or equivalent specific path), not a wildcard
Does NOT stage or mention .env as a file to commit
Shows the plan and asks for confirmation before executing

evals.name: message-quality-without-context
evals.description: Commit message quality when there is NO conversation context: the user says only 'commit' with no explanation. The skill must read the diff to infer a meaningful message — not produce a generic 'Update files' or ask the user what was changed.
evals.git_state: Modified: src/pricing/discount.py — the diff shows a bug fix: MAX_DISCOUNT_PERCENT was 150, changed to 100, preventing discounts from exceeding 100%
evals.conversation_context: None — user said only '/stepwise-git:commit' with no prior explanation of the change

assertions.text: Runs git diff to read the actual changes before drafting the commit message — does not ask the user what was changed
Commit message describes the specific fix (MAX_DISCOUNT_PERCENT cap, or preventing discounts over 100%) — not a generic 'Update discount.py' or 'Fix bug'
Subject line is NOT a vague message like 'Update files', 'Fix bug', 'Minor fix', or 'Update discount.py'
No Claude attribution in message

evals.name: shows-log-after-commit
evals.description: Post-commit output: after the user confirms and commits are created, the skill must show git log --oneline and suggest next steps.

assertions.text: After commit is created, runs 'git log --oneline' showing the new commit hash and message
Suggests at least one next step: review with git show, push to remote, or create PR
Mentions '/clear' as a tip to free up context for the next task

evals.name: nothing-to-commit-handles-gracefully
evals.description: Edge case: git status shows a clean working tree. Skill must report that there's nothing to commit without creating an empty commit or erroring.
evals.git_state: Clean working tree: no staged changes, no unstaged changes

assertions.text: Runs git status and identifies there are no changes to commit
Does NOT attempt to run git commit when there are no changes
Clearly informs the user that there is nothing to commit — does not error or silently succeed

grading_guide.capability_assertions: The output explicitly demonstrates the described behavior. Evidence must be present in the response or in the tool calls made — not inferred from context.
grading_guide.behavior_assertions: Binary: did the forbidden action happen or not? Check actual git commands issued, not just the plan text.
grading_guide.attribution_check: The no-attribution assertions are the highest-priority invariants. Any commit message containing 'Co-Authored-By', 'Generated with Claude', or 'Claude' in any casing is an automatic fail for that eval, regardless of other scores.
grading_guide.command_verification: For assertions about git add, inspect the actual Bash tool calls issued by the skill — not just the plan presented to the user. A plan saying 'I will add specific files' but then calling 'git add .' is a behavior failure.
grading_guide.statistical_requirements: With min_runs=3, report mean, stddev, min, max per assertion. The attribution and git-add-all assertions should score 1.0 in every run — any variance there signals a skill reliability problem.
